title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
prompt:
Design serialization: turn a tree into a string, and rebuild the exact tree from that string.

To make this testable here, implement private `serialize(TreeNode)` and `deserialize(String)` helpers; the graded method returns `deserialize(serialize(root))`, which must reproduce the tree exactly (including shape and negatives).

The clean approach: pre-order DFS writing `N` for nulls, e.g. `1,2,N,N,3,N,N`.
hints: Serialize with pre-order DFS, writing a sentinel (like `N`) for null children, comma-separated.
Deserialize by consuming tokens in the same pre-order: a token is a node (recurse for its two children) or `N` (return null).
A shared index into the token array drives the reconstruction.

solution.explanation: O(n) both ways. Pre-order with explicit null markers is self-delimiting: reading a value means 'build a node and its two subtrees come next', reading `N` means 'empty' — so the same left-then-right recursion that wrote the string reads it back into the identical shape.
